description: Create the base Python trading bot repository with modular folders for data, strategy, risk, execution, ML, backtesting, monitoring, deployment, and tests.
inputs: Target exchange: Binance Futures or exchange-agnostic adapter

description: Build a centralized configuration system for API credentials, symbols, timeframe settings, risk limits, Silver Bullet session windows, paper/live mode, and ML model toggles.
inputs: Trading pair list such as BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT
outputs: Validation errors for missing or unsafe settings

description: Create an abstract exchange adapter interface so the bot can support Binance Futures first while remaining extensible to other exchanges later.
outputs: Methods for fetching candles, balances, positions, orders, and placing/canceling orders

description: Implement historical OHLCV data acquisition for backtesting and ML dataset creation. Store clean candle data locally using Parquet or SQLite.
Build a live candle stream module using exchange WebSocket data with automatic reconnect, heartbeat checks, and fallback REST polling.
Create a local data storage layer for candles, signals, trades, backtest results, ML features, model predictions, bot logs, and performance metrics.

Implement the ICT Silver Bullet session scheduler using America/New_York timezone with DST awareness. The common Silver Bullet windows are London 03:00-04:00, New York AM 10:00-11:00, and New York PM 14:00-15:00 New York time. Sources describe the model as time-based and centered around liquidity and Fair Value Gaps.

Build market structure detection for swing highs, swing lows, break of structure, change of character, and market structure shift. This module will support Silver Bullet confirmation after liquidity has been swept.
outputs: Swing high and swing low labels

description: Detect external liquidity levels such as previous session high, previous session low, previous day high, previous day low, equal highs, equal lows, and recent swing liquidity.

Implement Fair Value Gap detection. For bullish FVG, detect three-candle imbalances where candle 1 high is below candle 3 low. For bearish FVG, detect cases where candle 1 low is above candle 3 high. FVGs are a core component of the Silver Bullet model.
Detect strong displacement candles after liquidity sweeps. Use candle body size, ATR multiple, volume expansion, and directional impulse to confirm that price moved with strength.

Create higher-timeframe bias logic using 1H, 4H, and 1D structure. The bot should avoid low-quality Silver Bullet trades that contradict major market direction unless configured for reversal-only mode.

Implement the full ICT Silver Bullet rule engine. Valid long setup: inside Silver Bullet window, sell-side liquidity swept, bullish displacement/MSS appears, bullish FVG forms, price retraces into FVG, target is nearest buy-side liquidity. Valid short setup is the inverse.

Create a deterministic signal scoring system before ML is introduced. Score each setup based on liquidity quality, FVG size, displacement strength, HTF alignment, session timing, spread, volatility, and reward-to-risk.
Build a hard risk management engine that calculates position size, validates stop-loss distance, blocks unsafe trades, and enforces daily risk limits.
Implement post-entry trade management, including partial take profit, break-even stop movement, trailing stop option, time-based exit, and session-end exit.
Create a safe execution engine for paper and live trading. It must place entries, stop-loss orders, take-profit orders, cancel stale orders, and handle rejected or partially filled orders.
Implement paper trading that simulates live execution using real-time market data without placing real orders. Include realistic slippage, fees, spreads, and partial fill simulation.
Build an event-driven backtesting engine that uses historical candles to simulate the full bot lifecycle, including session windows, entries, exits, fees, slippage, risk limits, and trade management.

Add validation tools to reduce false confidence. Include out-of-sample testing, walk-forward testing, Monte Carlo trade reshuffling, fee sensitivity, slippage sensitivity, and symbol-by-symbol analysis.
Create a supervised ML dataset from historical Silver Bullet setups. Each row should represent one valid or near-valid setup with engineered features and a future outcome label.
outputs: Labels such as win/loss, max favorable excursion, max adverse excursion, realized R multiple

description: Engineer ML features for trade filtering. Include session type, time inside session, FVG size, distance to liquidity, ATR, displacement strength, volume expansion, HTF trend, spread, funding rate if available, and recent volatility regime.

Train baseline ML models to act only as a probability filter, not as the main trader. Start with Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost or LightGBM if available. Predict probability that a setup reaches target before stop-loss.
Integrate the trained ML model into the live strategy pipeline. The model should only approve, reject, or downsize rule-based Silver Bullet signals. It must not generate trades independently.
Create a simple model registry to track ML model versions, training periods, features used, validation results, and deployment status.

Build an optional AI analyst module that summarizes bot performance, reviews trade journals, detects repeated failure patterns, and suggests parameter reviews. The AI agent must not place trades directly.
Implement Telegram alerts for bot status, detected setups, trade entries, exits, errors, daily loss lockout, exchange disconnects, and performance summaries.
Create a lightweight local dashboard using Streamlit, FastAPI, or a simple web UI to monitor equity curve, open positions, daily PnL, win rate, drawdown, active model version, and recent trades.
Build structured logging for all bot decisions. Every trade must record why it was entered, why it was rejected, what rules passed, what rules failed, and what the ML probability was.

Implement emergency safety controls. The bot must stop opening new trades after max daily loss, max consecutive losses, API errors, abnormal slippage, repeated rejected orders, or manual kill switch activation.
Write unit tests for FVG detection, liquidity sweep detection, MSS detection, position sizing, session conversion, risk lockout, order validation, and ML feature generation.
Create integration tests that simulate the complete bot flow from candle input to signal generation, risk approval, paper execution, trade management, and database logging.
Containerize the bot using Docker. Include separate commands for backtesting, paper trading, live trading, dashboard, and ML training.

Prepare deployment scripts for running the bot 24/7 on a free or low-cost VPS such as Oracle Cloud Always Free. Include Docker setup, firewall rules, log rotation, restart policy, and environment setup.
Create a systemd or supervisor service to keep the bot running continuously, restart it after crashes, and start it automatically after VPS reboot.
Implement security practices for API keys and environment secrets. Ensure secrets are never committed to GitHub. Support read-only, trade-only, and withdrawal-disabled API keys.

Create a pre-live checklist that blocks live trading unless all requirements are met: profitable out-of-sample backtest, stable paper trading, kill switch enabled, Telegram alerts working, correct leverage, and withdrawal disabled on API keys.
Enable live trading only after the readiness checklist passes. Live mode must use conservative default risk, isolated margin, strict stop-loss placement, and no martingale logic.
Generate an automated daily report showing trades taken, rejected setups, PnL, drawdown, win rate, average R, best trade, worst trade, rule failures, and ML filter decisions.

Create an optional retraining pipeline that retrains the ML filter using newly collected trade and market data. New models must not replace the active model unless validation metrics improve out-of-sample.

Build a constrained optimizer for strategy parameters such as FVG minimum size, liquidity lookback, ATR threshold, stop buffer, RR minimum, and ML probability threshold. The optimizer must use walk-forward validation and must not optimize directly on the final test set.
Extend the bot to monitor multiple symbols while enforcing portfolio-level risk limits, correlation controls, and maximum simultaneous trades.

Maintain and finalize project documentation as the bot is developed. Documentation should explain architecture, setup, strategy rules, backtesting, paper trading, live deployment, risk rules, ML model usage, monitoring, and emergency shutdown procedures.
